newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech SPT Telecom announces tariff hike.
newsitem.headline: Czech SPT Telecom announces tariff hike.

text.p: Czech telecommunications company SPT Telecom a.s. said on Monday it had received approval from the finance ministry to raise prices by a nominal average of four percent with effect from April 1, 1997.

"The average total price increase of SPT Telecom's regulated services amounts to four percent, which is well below the estimated inflation rate in 1997 of over nine percent," SPT Telecom said in a statement.
SPT detailed the following changes to its tariff structure:
* Local calls will be increased to 2.25 crowns from 2.0 per pulse. The length of the pulses remains unchanged.
* Domestic long distance zone one (adjacent areas) will be abolished and replaced by local call prices. Effectively this means a substantial price decrease, SPT said.

* All other domestic long distance calls will be increased to 2.25 crowns from 2.0 per pulse. However, by changing the duration of the domestic long distance pulse, the average price paid for these calls will remain unchanged.
* The increase of fixed monthly charges for single lines will rise to 90 crowns from 80. Monthly charges for double lines will rise to 54 crowns from 48 and group lines to 17 crowns from 15.
* Peak hours on weekdays will be extended to 7 am-6 pm from 7 am-4 pm.
* Payphone prices will rise to three crowns per pulse from two.
* Prices for international calls including to Slovakia remain effectively unchanged.
"The price adjustment is necessary to ensure SPT Telecom's ambitious network and quality development programme," the company said.

SPT Telecom has accelerated efforts to expand and improve its communist-era network since Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV and Swiss Telecom together bought 27 percent of the company last year from the government for $1.32 billion plus $141 million in additional services.
This involves the installation of 400,000 telephone lines this year and almost one million in 1997 and 1998. By the end of 1998, applications for lines will be served within a few weeks, SPT said.
